chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda, who said:

When the woman sees the purity (end of menstruation) and the time of the prayer has entered upon her, then she delays the ritual bath (ghusl) until the time for another prayer enters, upon her is the making up (qada) of that prayer which she neglected. So when she becomes clean during the time of the obligation of the prayer, and she delays the prayer until the time for another prayer comes, then she sees blood, upon her is the making up of that prayer which she neglected.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up prayers if a woman delays her ritual bath after menstruation ends?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith clarifies the specific condition under which a menstruating woman incurs the obligation of *qada* (making up) a missed prayer: only when she delays her *ghusl* beyond the prayer's time while still in a state of purity. It distinguishes this from merely delaying the prayer itself after becoming pure, highlighting the juristic principle that the delay in purification is the primary cause for the missed prayer's liability. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on timely ritual preparation as a prerequisite for valid worship.
